case_title: Anuj Singh v. State of Bihar
statutory_provisions: IPC s.324, s.34; Arms Act s.27
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s. 307 rw s. 34 and s. 27 of the Arms Act
high_court_outcome: Modified conviction to s. 324 and s. 27 of the Arms Act
offence_finally_established: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapon under s. 324 IPC and s. 27 of the Arms Act
neutral_facts: The prosecution case is that the accused, who were neighbors, had a land dispute with the victim. On the day of the incident, the victim was repairing his wall when the accused approached him, leading to an altercation. The accused, armed with firearms and other weapons, fired upon the victim, causing injuries to his left foot and right arm. The victim was taken to a clinic where medical evidence confirmed that the injuries were caused by firearms. Witnesses testified that the accused were present at the scene with weapons and that the victim sustained injuries as a result of the altercation. The medical evidence corroborated that the injuries were caused by firearms, and the prosecution argued that the accused used the weapons due to the ongoing dispute.
